resources.string: Background limits by version and manufacturer

This screen gathers the background limits: what each component in our implementation can do, what changes in each Android version, and what each manufacturer blocks. Where needed, there are buttons that open the relevant settings screen.
Limits by manufacturer (Don\'t kill my app)
No matching settings screen was found on this device
Does the schedule survive and self-heal

On every open the app checks whether the schedule exists, and if not, re-creates it and records that. After the device boots, the BootReceiver re-creates it. A failed run still schedules the next one. There is no continuous background watchdog: if the system stops the schedule while the app is closed and there is no boot, it is restored only on the next open.

This deletes all recorded runs and the succeeded / failed / boot counts, so you can test from a clean slate. The schedule and settings are kept. This can\'t be undone.

A working test URL is set by default, so the app sends out of the box. Tap \"Create a fresh link\" for a new one with its own quota — it is saved automatically, no need to press Save URL. Only the last URL is used; with auto-renew on, the app makes a new one by itself when the current one runs out.
